summary.text: St. Chrysogonus was St. Anastasia’s Christian teacher and is remembered as a martyr executed at Aquileia under Diocletian.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: The OCA’s life of St. Anastasia identifies St. Chrysogonus as her learned Christian teacher. His name is also transliterated Chrysogonos. The narrative places him within the persecutions associated with Diocletian, rather than describing him as a later medieval Roman figure.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: When St. Anastasia is confined by her husband, the account says that she secretly corresponds with her teacher. He encourages steadfastness in Christ. Later the emperor orders imprisoned Christians killed and has Chrysogonus sent to Aquileia for questioning. The correspondence and imprisonment belong to the received hagiographical account.
blocks.locator: Secret correspondence and transfer to Aquileia

blocks.text: According to that life, the emperor cannot induce him to deny Christ and orders his beheading. His body is thrown into the sea, washed ashore and recovered for honorable keeping. These events are attributed to the published ecclesiastical narrative, not expanded with invented dates or dialogue.

blocks.text: The OCA names St. Chrysogonus in the December 22 commemoration with St. Anastasia. His place in her story illustrates the support offered by an imprisoned teacher to another Christian under pressure. His Orthodox recognition is explicit in that calendar entry.
